study type: analytical cross-sectional study with prospective data collection
cohort: The study included 122 women experiencing Severe Ante Partum Hemorrhage (SAPH) out of 7,469 women admitted in obstetrics.
finding: Severe Ante Partum Hemorrhage (SAPH) represented 1.6% of hospitalizations and was associated with significant maternal (15.6% of all maternal deaths) and fetal (18.1% perinatal deaths in SAPH cases) morbidity and mortality, with evacuation, critical clinical condition, and uterine rupture being associated with poor outcomes.
